title: Belantamab Mafodotin in Multiple Myeloma: Molecular Mechanisms, Immunobiology, Resistance, and Clinical Repositioning
content: Belantamab mafodotin, a B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-targeted antibody–drug conjugate (ADC), has emerged as an important therapeutic option in the evolving treatment landscape of multiple myeloma (MM). Its clinical development has pro-gressed from single-agent activity in heavily pretreated patients to combination strate-gies demonstrating significant clinical benefit in relapsed/refractory disease. This narra-tive review provides an integrated overview of the molecular structure, mechanisms of action, immunobiological effects, resistance pathways, toxicity profile, and evolving clinical positioning of belantamab mafodotin. Preclinical studies support multiple complementary mechanisms, including direct cytotoxicity through intracellular delivery of monomethyl auristatin F (MMAF), antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, anti-body-dependent cellular phagocytosis, and immunogenic cell death. The contribution of immunogenic cell death and other effects on the tumor microenvironment to clinical benefit remains unproven. Potential resistance mechanisms include alterations in BCMA expression, impaired intracellular processing, payload-related resistance, and changes in immune effector function. The characteristic ocular toxicity, particularly keratopathy, remains the principal treatment-limiting adverse effect and reflects, at least partly, BCMA-independent uptake of the ADC by corneal epithelial cells. Clinical evidence from the phase III DREAMM-7 and DREAMM-8 trials has established the efficacy of belantamab-containing combinations, with significant improvements in progres-sion-free survival compared with their respective control regimens. In contrast, bel-antamab mafodotin monotherapy did not demonstrate superiority for the primary progression-free survival endpoint of DREAMM-3. Emerging combination strategies, including regimens incorporating immunomodulatory drugs, proteasome inhibitors, and γ-secretase inhibitors, may further expand its therapeutic applications. Meanwhile, the optimal sequencing of belantamab mafodotin with BCMA-directed chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies and bispecific antibodies remains unresolved. Overall, bel-antamab mafodotin represents an evolving BCMA-targeted treatment strategy in MM. Future research should focus on identifying predictive biomarkers, optimizing dosing schedules to minimize ocular toxicity, defining effective combination approaches, and establishing evidence-based sequencing strategies to maximize clinical benefit.
